'''Note:''' Community history is messy. This page prefers '''dated primary or archived sources''' and labels secondary/uncertain claims. It does '''not''' invent backstory. For rules-by-era see [[Rulebooks]]; for constructed pools see [[Formats]]; for virtual packaging eras see [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]] vs [[:Category:Virtual Legacy sets|Virtual Blocks]] vs [[:Category:Current Virtual sets|Current Virtual]].

The '''History of the Players Committee''' traces how volunteer Players Committee (PC) support replaced Decipher's commercial end-of-life for ''Star Wars'' CCG, created Virtual cards, reorganized them, and later Reset the tournament pool.

This wiki is a '''fan encyclopedia'''. It is not the Players Committee and does not replace [https://www.starwarsccg.org/ starwarsccg.org].

== Timeline (high level) ==

=== Decipher era and handoff ===

Decipher published ''Star Wars'' CCG from 1995 through [[Theed Palace]] (2001) and related products. When Decipher announced the license was leaving, it publicly formed a '''Players' Committee''' / Player Advocate structure so fans could continue organized play, rulings, and support.<ref name="pc1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611042314/http://decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002; letter dated 25 January 2002)</ref>

'''Decipher call for volunteers:''' Decipher's Star Wars Announcement page invited players to '''volunteer for the players' committee''' (volunteer contact listed on that page) alongside Holland/Jones and Lucas Licensing contacts, and linked the '''01.25.02''' Players' Committee announcement.<ref name="deciphercall">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020601152726/http://decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html The Star Wars Announcement], decipher.com (Wayback, 1 June 2002)</ref> The PC Advocates originated from that Decipher call for volunteers / committee formation.

On '''25 January 2002''', Warren Holland (Chairman &amp; CEO) announced the '''first team of Star Wars Player Advocates''' on Decipher's Players' Committee page (Wayback capture of that HTML: 11 June 2002).<ref name="pc1" /> That letter names early Advocate roles (player support, tournament support, rules support, gameplay support), describes a Norfolk meeting to turn the game over to players, notes Game Players Network assistance with communications and prize shipping after 30 April 2002, and teases a forthcoming virtual-card pool and timetable.<ref name="pc1" />

Named Advocates (including person pages for the first six and early Council figures such as [[Doug Taylor]], [[Josh Radke]], and [[John Arendt]]) and later Advocate Council rosters are collected on [[Players Committee advocates]]. Dated PC organization chart PDFs (2021 Wayback / 2024 live) supply later name/handle Advocate rows on that hub.

Contemporary fan indexes (GPN) tracked PC news in spring 2002, including a '''29 April 2002''' headline that Decipher would donate over one million dollars in product, promotional materials, and financial backing to the Players Committee.<ref name="gpn2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610202816/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/games.asp?gm=starwars Game Players Network - Star Wars CCG index], Wayback 10 June 2002</ref>

=== Virtual program begins (2002) ===

The PC's '''first Virtual Card Set''' was announced to the community on '''12 February 2002''' (TFN citing GPN), with a targeted release of '''4 March 2002''' and Virtual Set #2 targeted for '''6 May 2002'''. Preview week was listed as 25 February-1 March 2002; distribution was via PDF on decipher.com.<ref name="tfn2002">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.Net, 12 February 2002</ref>

Decipher's "Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!" page (dated '''5 March 2002''') describes twelve Premiere-based (V) slips and states the cards would be '''tournament-legal Saturday, 9 March 2002'''.<ref name="decivs1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], decipher.com (Wayback)</ref>

Early printable framing is preserved in [https://web.archive.org/web/20050813215254/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/virtual/VirtualCards1.pdf VirtualCards1.pdf]. That '''modifier / sleeve presentation is very different''' from later Block-era and current Virtual packaging - see [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]].

From 2002 into 2009 the PC continued releasing '''numbered Virtual Sets''' (and [[Defensive Shields]] in secondary chronologies; soft-label Premium Set 1 historical). See the set index on [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]] for what is sourced versus still unmarked.

=== Reorg / "Blocks" (about September 2009) ===

Full hub: [[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]] (also [[Virtual Sets to Virtual Blocks]]).

Block PDFs: '''reorganization of the previous 18 virtual sets''' into six thematic blocks; '''Official text as of 7 December 2009'''.<ref name="blockreorg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf VirtualBlock1.pdf]</ref> Aug/Sep 2009 soft announce; Dec stamp is firm. Pre-reorg dating: [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]. Later Block slices continue (e.g. Polish chronology lists Block 6.3 Mercenaries '''15 March 2010''' -- post-reorg, not a VS1-18 ship date).

The Players Committee later regrouped Legacy Virtual material into '''Virtual Blocks''' (2009-2014). The official slips library still labels '''Legacy Virtual Sets (2002-2009)''' separately from '''Legacy Virtual Blocks (2009-2014)'''.<ref name="slips">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Virtual Slips / Files], starwarsccg.org</ref>

On this wiki, Block hubs are [[Virtual Block 1]]-[[Virtual Block 9]] and [[Virtual Shields]]. Era overview: [[Virtual Legacy]]. '''Do not treat Blocks as a lossless rename of VS1-18:''' presentation, organization, errata, and the legal card pool could change, and Virtual cards could be '''dropped''' relatively easily compared with reprinting physical product. Exact drop lists and modifier diffs need cited sources page-by-page (planned later).

Terms such as community "Redux" / "Revolution" appear in period set naming (for example secondary lists call Virtual Set 3 "Revolution") but this page does '''not''' equate marketing nicknames with the 2009 Block reorg unless a primary source says so.

=== Advanced Rulebook 2.0 (Legacy Virtual rules) ===

During the Legacy Virtual period the PC published [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0]] (archived final PDF; wiki transcription labeled Legacy Virtual-era). Among other revisions it introduced the [[Mission]] card type. That book is '''not''' the current tournament Advanced Rulebook.

=== 2014 Virtual Card Reset ===

Reset '''announce ~14 July 2014''' (Category One-era reporting; '''med''' pending stable permalink). Wiki [[Virtual Set 0]] / [[Virtual Set D]] = '''24 September 2014'''. Oct 2014 community summaries discuss the new pool.

In '''Fall 2014''' the PC Reset the competitive virtual pool. On this wiki, [[Virtual Set 0]] and [[Virtual Set D]] are dated '''24 September 2014''' on the Main Page Current Virtual band. The Alternate Format Tournament Guide describes '''Standard''' (post-Reset virtual icons) versus '''Legacy''' (pre-Reset black-diamond / Block pool), and notes the 2014 World Championships as the last championship circuit on the old pool.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), via [[Formats]]</ref>

After the Reset, Current Virtual sets continue (see [[:Category:Current Virtual sets]]). Current tournament rules are transcribed at [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]] (2023 edition).

=== Current site ===

An early official Players Committee website was at '''swccgpc.com'''. A Wayback Machine capture dated '''6 November 2002''' presents [https://web.archive.org/web/20021106101746/http://www.swccgpc.com/ The SWCCG Player's Committee] as the official website for the Star Wars Customizable Card Game (page content includes October 2002 news; contact tournaments@swccgpc.com).<ref name="swccgpc2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106101746/http://www.swccgpc.com/ The SWCCG Player's Committee], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 6 November 2002)</ref> This page does not invent a domain launch date beyond what that capture shows.

On '''10 June 2009''', PC news "New Domain and Server" announced that the committee had completed moving to a new server and was forwarding to its new domain at '''StarWarsCCG.org''' (starwarsccg.org), noting expected hiccups and asking users to report issues on the forums.<ref name="domain2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706102740/http://www.starwarsccg.org/news/news.php?id=69 New Domain and Server], starwarsccg.org news.php?id=69 (posted 10 June 2009; Wayback capture 6 July 2009)</ref>

Organized play, slips, formats, and news remain at [https://www.starwarsccg.org/ starwarsccg.org]. This wiki cross-links those resources but does not replace them.

'''Errata and drops:''' Virtual text is easier to revise or remove from legality than a physical print run. A card's (V) text in 2002, its Block-era presentation, and any current Virtual descendant may disagree. Prefer the document and format that match the era you are playing; do not assume "whatever is on the current cardlist" is the historical text.

== Gaps and uncertainties ==

* '''Redux / Re-Edit''' primary program pages still thin; V7-11 "Official text as of 4 Dec 2006" is not proven first ship ([[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]).
* '''Modern starwarsccg.org takeover / org-transfer story: still UNKNOWN''' as a full cutover narrative. Domain/server move is cited: on '''10 June 2009''' PC news "New Domain and Server" announced completed move to a new server and forwarding to starwarsccg.org (Wayback of news.php?id=69).<ref name="domain2009" /> Earlier HTML archival also showed the domain forward by 5 July 2009; that remains secondary corroboration only.
* Drop-lists between pre-reorg / Block / Reset: known in principle, '''not tabulated yet'''.
* Soft Aug/Sep 2009 Block announce URLs vs '''7 Dec 2009''' PDF stamp; '''~14 Jul 2014''' Reset announce permalink.

* Exact legal dates for most of VS3-VS18 and Defensive Shields are '''not yet cited''' from primary announces on this wiki.
* Whether every secondary subtitle (star-wars.pl) matches PC marketing names needs confirmation against slip covers/announces.
* VS18 appears on a secondary list but is not named in the PC slips "Sets 1-17" heading cited above.
* Community nicknames (Redux, Revolution, etc.) are only partially pinned to primary PC terminology here.
* Full inventories of cards '''dropped''' between pre-reorg, Block, and Reset pools are out of scope until sourced.
